<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par151 />{{GHGheb|text=מִי גַם־בָּכֶם וְיִסְגֹּר דְּלָתַ֫יִם|translate=would that one were among you and would shut the doors}}, i.e. O that one would shut the doors!

{{GHGmargin-letter|151|b}}
Rem. Sometimes the original sense of {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יִתֵּן}} is still plainly discernible, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=29}} {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יִתֵּן אֶת־הָעָם הַזֶּה בְיָדִי|translate=who gives this people into my hand?}} equivalent to, O that this people were given into my hand! cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=7}}. In these examples, however, {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יִתֵּן}} is still equivalent to ''O had I!'' and in numerous other instances the idea of ''giving'' has entirely disappeared, {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יִתֵּן}} having become stereotyped as a mere desiderative particle (''utinam''). Its construction is either—

(''a'') With the ''accusative'' (in accordance with its original meaning) of a substantive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=67}} ''would that it were even!... morning!'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=14|verse=7}} (53:7), 55:7; with an accusative and a following infinitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=5}}; with two accusatives, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=8|verse=23}}; with the accusative of an infinitive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=16|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יִתֵּן מוּתִי אֲנִי תַחְתֶּ֫יךָ|translate=would that I had died for thee}} (for {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} cf. {{GHGpar|135|f}}); of a participle, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=35}}; of a personal pronoun (as a suffix), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=2}} (with a following {{GHGheb|text=כְּ}}; but {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יִתְּנֵ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=4}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=9|verse=1}} with a following accusative is not simply equivalent to {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יִתֵּן לִי}}, but is properly ''who endows me with'', &c.; cf. {{GHGpar|117|ff}}).—With a still greater weakening of the original meaning {{GHGheb|text=מִֽי־יִתֵּן}} is used with an adjective in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=4}} ''could a clean thing but come out of an unclean!'' i.e. ''how can a clean thing come'', &c.; similarly in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=31}} ''who can find one that hath not been satisfied!''

{{GHGmargin-letter|151|c}}
(''b'') With a following perfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=23|verse=3}} (cf. {{GHGpar|120|e}}); with a perfect consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=26}} ''O that they had such an heart!''

{{GHGmargin-letter|151|d}}
(''c'') With a following imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=13|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=13|hidebook=1}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=23}} the imperfect is twice added with {{GHGterm|Wāw}} (cf. ''a'' above, on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mal.|chapter=1|verse=10}}).

On the cohortative in the apodosis to such desiderative clauses, cf. {{GHGpar|108|f}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|151|e}}
'''2.''' The wish may also be expressed by the particles {{GHGheb|text=אִם}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=81|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=95|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=24|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=4|verse=10}}; always with a following imperfect) and {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} (for which in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=5}} we have {{GHGheb|text=אַחְלַי}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=אַֽחֲלֵי}}, from {{GHGheb|text=אָח|translate=ah!}} and {{GHGheb|text=לַי}}={{GHGheb|text=לוּ}}; both with a following imperfect) ''si, o si! utinam''.<ref>Cf. a similar transition from a conditional to a desiderative particle, in consequence of the suppression of the apodosis, in the English, ''O if I had!'' and the like; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=29}} ''if there were'' ({{GHGheb|text=לוּ יֶשׁ־}}) ''a sword in my hand now had I surely killed thee!''</ref> {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} is followed by the imperfect, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=2}}; by the jussive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=34}} (rather concessive, equivalent to ''let it be so''); by the perfect, as the expression of a wish that something might have happened in past time (cf. {{GHGpar|106|p}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=לוּ מַ֫תְנוּ|translate=would that we had died}}; 20:3 and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=7|verse=7}} (both times {{GHGheb|text=וְלוּ}}); on the other hand, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=48|verse=18}} and 63:19 (both times {{GHGheb|text=לוּא}}) to express a wish that something expected in the future may already have happened.—On {{GHGheb|text=לוּ}} with the imperative (by an anacoluthon) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=23|verse=13}} cf. {{GHGpar|110|e}}. On the perfect after {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=5|verse=20}}, cf. {{GHGpar|106|n}}, note 2.<section end=par151 /><noinclude>
